newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA WIN TO CLOSE IN ON JUVENTUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA WIN TO CLOSE IN ON JUVENTUS.

text.p: Argentine Hernan Crespo and Massimo Crippa were both on target as second-place Parma came from behind to win 2-1 at Perugia on Sunday and close Juventus's lead at the top of the Italian league to four points.

But pacesetters Juve will restore their grip on the championship, and take a giant step toward a record 24th league title, if they avoid defeat against third-placed Inter at the San Siro later in the day.
Fourth-placed Sampdoria's faltering title challenge suffered another blow with a 4-0 thrashing at Atalanta that left them eight points adrift of Juventus.
The league's leading scorer Filippo Inzaghi scored a hat-trick for Atalanta to take his season's tally to 18, while Sampdoria's Yugoslav sweeper Sinisa Mihajlovic was shown a red card for dissent.

Fiorentina followed up their 2-0 win at Benfica in last week's European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final by twice recovering from a goal down to defeat sixth-placed Bologna 3-2 -- their first league win in two months.
French defender Vincent Candela lifted Roma into fifth place with an 89th minute winner -- his second goal of the match -- in his side's 4-3 victory over Verona at the Olympic stadium.
